title: Pork Faggots in Gravy
subtitle: A Midlands classic of herbed pork meatballs braised in rich onion gravy
excerpt: Pork mince shaped into round faggots with sage and onion, then braised low and slow in a dark beef gravy. A proper British comfort dish that is best made a day ahead.
sourceNotes: Midlands British tradition adapted for a standard roasting tin on the hob and oven.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the faggots in their gravy. Defrost overnight and reheat gently on the hob.
recipe.batchNotes: This recipe doubles well. Freeze in portions for a ready-made comfort supper.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day ahead and refrigerate in the gravy. The flavour improves overnight.

content.text: Faggots are made from pork mince mixed with breadcrumbs, onion and sage, then shaped into round balls and braised in a deep onion gravy. The braising liquid keeps them moist throughout the long cook. Serve with mashed potato and mushy peas for the full Midlands experience.

items.prepNote: 2 finely grated for the mix, 1 sliced for the gravy

content.text: Mix the pork mince, breadcrumbs, grated onion, sage, beaten egg and plenty of salt and black pepper together in the large bowl. Combine well with your hands.
Shape into 8 round balls, roughly the size of a golf ball. Set aside on a plate.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Brown the faggots all over in batches, about 3 minutes per batch. Transfer to the roasting tin.
In the same pan, cook the sliced onion over a low heat for 10 minutes until soft. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beef stock and worcestershire sauce. Stir well and bring to the boil. Season and pour over the faggots in the roasting tin.
Heat the oven to 170C. Cover the tin tightly with foil. Bake for 45 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for a further 15 minutes so the tops colour and the gravy thickens.
Rest for 10 minutes. Serve with mashed potato and mushy peas with plenty of gravy poured over.

items.symptom: The faggots break apart during cooking.
items.cause: The mix was too dry, or the breadcrumbs and egg were not worked in properly.
items.fix: Make sure the mix is well combined and holds together when squeezed. Add a splash more beaten egg if the mixture feels crumbly.

items.cause: Not enough flour was cooked in at the onion stage.
items.fix: Mix a tablespoon of cornflour with 2 tablespoons of cold water. Stir into the gravy and return to a low heat until thickened.

items.symptom: The outsides are pale and soft.
items.cause: The faggots were not browned properly before going into the oven.
items.fix: Give them a full 2 to 3 minutes per side in the pan before transferring. Good colour here adds flavour throughout the braise.
